package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via automatic updates of legitimate Windows applications)
package_info.package_versions: Current version as of June 2022 (exact version not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: WinDealer is an information stealer malware used by the LuoYu APT group. It is delivered through automatic updates of legitimate applications and enables attackers to search and transmit data from infected Windows systems, install backdoors for persistence, manipulate files, propagate, and execute arbitrary commands. Its primary purpose is unauthorized data exfiltration and system compromise.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into legitimate application process or dropped as a separate executable

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code searches the filesystem for sensitive files, then transmits matching files to a command-and-control server, resulting in data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated searching and exfiltration of user files to an external server is a hallmark of infostealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications should not scan for sensitive files and transmit them to unknown remote servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise backup or cloud sync tools may upload user files, but only to trusted, user-configured destinations.
key_indicators: Automated file search for sensitive patterns

execution_context.file_location: Windows registry (Run key) or scheduled task

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Pseudocode representation
reg add HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run /v WinDealer /t REG_SZ /d "C:\Users\user\AppData\Roaming\winupdater.exe"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code creates a registry entry to ensure the malware is executed at every system startup, establishing persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Adding persistence via registry keys is a common malware tactic to survive reboots.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not silently add itself to autorun without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate updaters or system utilities may use autorun for updates.
key_indicators: Non-standard executable path (e.g., winupdater.exe in AppData)

execution_context.file_location: Injected code in memory or dropped script

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving a command from the C2 server, the code executes arbitrary commands on the infected system, enabling remote control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote command execution from an external server is a core capability of backdoors and RATs.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications should not accept and execute arbitrary remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools, but only with strong authentication and user awareness.

attack_chain.action: Malware is delivered via automatic update of a legitimate application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial infection and execution of malicious code

attack_chain.action: Malware searches for sensitive files and exfiltrates them to the attacker's C2 server.
Malware establishes persistence by modifying registry keys or creating scheduled tasks.
Malware receives and executes arbitrary commands from the C2 server, enabling further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote control and potential lateral movement

behavioral_signatures: Legitimate application processes making unexpected outbound connections to unknown domains
Automated enumeration and exfiltration of user files
Creation of persistence mechanisms (registry Run keys, scheduled tasks) by non-updater processes
Execution of arbitrary commands received from remote servers
file_indicators: Unexpected executables in AppData or Temp directories (e.g., winupdater.exe)
Registry Run keys referencing non-standard binaries
Injected code in memory of legitimate processes
network_indicators: Outbound connections to attacker-controlled C2 infrastructure (domains/IPs not associated with legitimate vendors)
Unusual data uploads from non-networking applications
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for legitimate applications initiating unexpected outbound network connections, especially to untrusted domains. Detect automated file access and exfiltration patterns. Alert on creation of persistence mechanisms (registry Run keys, scheduled tasks) by processes not associated with system updates. Monitor for execution of commands received from external sources, and correlate with known C2 infrastructure.
